Thanks Ben & Priya — great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the SLO/Autoscale ask from FastPay: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Target 95th pctl latency: 150ms for single-turn generation (avg token size ~12 tokens).
- Burst scenarios: marketing campaigns + payroll processing peaks where QPS jumps 5–7x for ~4–8 minutes.
- Required concurrency: sustained 120 concurrent requests during peak windows, with short spikes to 400 concurrent for <10 minutes.
- Streaming: client requires server-sent partial token streaming for low-latency UX (no chunking >200ms).
- Warm pools: would prefer a warm pool to handle spikes — minimize cold-starts to under 2s for new compute.

Open items (action owners):
1) Redwood: provide SLO qualification worksheet + proposed autoscale config (warm pool size, scale-up timings, queueing behavior) — Marissa/Connor by EOD Thursday 3/31.
2) FastPay: share historical QPS traces (15s granularity) and a representative prompt set for perf testing — Ben/Priya by Friday 4/1.
3) Joint: schedule a tech deep-dive to validate KV cache behavior and streaming performance with Connor & Ethan — proposed 4/2 10am PT.

Attachments: I attached an SLO_worksheet template and a quick warm-pool diagram. Please flag any corrections.

Thanks Marissa — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- The 95th pctl target is for end-to-end user-facing latency; we can tolerate up to 200ms at 95th for text-only flows but prefer 150ms for chat flows with streaming.
- Spikes: the short spikes to 400 concurrency are usually very bursty — typically <6 minutes. We do care about tail behavior more than average.
- Cold starts: 2s is a hard target if possible; anything above ~4s requires client-side UX changes.

Thanks all — quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow's deep-dive: 

1) Autoscaling behavior we propose:
   - Warm pool: maintain 40 pre-warmed workers (model-variant specific) to absorb short spikes.
   - Scale-up: policy to add 50 workers/minute with aggressive burst mode (adds up to additional 200 workers in first 3 minutes) when queue depth > 30.
   - Queueing: soft-queue with prioritization for streaming sessions (so partial tokens are flushed ASAP), and backpressure to clients when queue exceeds 200 requests.

2) Cold-starts:
   - Cold-start for a new GPU instance measured on comparable infra is ~3.5–4s for full model load; warm pool cuts that to <400ms for request-ready.

3) Streaming constraints:
   - Our streaming pipeline offers sub-100ms token flush in steady state; during scale events, we prioritize streaming sessions on warm pool workers to keep perceived latency low.

Questions for FastPay before the call:
- Can you confirm the proportion of streaming vs batch (non-streaming) requests during peaks?
- Are there any regulatory constraints (e.g., region-specific routing) that affect warm pool placement?

I'll bring a short perf-run checklist and a small test harness to the deep-dive so we can reproduce tail latency and concurrency profiles.

Connor O'Brien
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — confirmed for the 4/2 deep-dive at 10am PT. Quick responses to Connor's questions and next steps: 

- Streaming vs batch: FastPay indicated ~70% of peak requests are streaming chat-style sessions. We'll prioritize those in the warm pool.
- Regional constraints: Ben confirmed most traffic is US-west with a small EU subset; no strict restrictions on warm-pool placement beyond data residency for EU traffic.

Updated autoscale proposal (summary):
- Warm pool: 50 pre-warmed workers in us-west to cover ~60% of typical short spikes.
- Aggressive burst add: +250 workers in first 4 minutes if queue depth triggers; subsequent linear scale thereafter.
- Soft-queue threshold: start applying backpressure beyond 250 queued requests; ability to prioritize streaming sessions so token flushes aren't blocked.
- SLO targets: aim for 95th pctl <= 150ms for chat (streaming) and <=200ms for text-only flows during steady state; during the first 2 minutes of a rare massive surge we allow a short tail increase up to 300ms while warm pool scales.
